videos.title: Why Inference Matters 12x More Than Training | YC Paper Club
videos.description:
This week’s Paper Club is all about inference. 

For every FLOP spent training a model, roughly six go to serving it each year — and getting that part right has produced over $220 billion in market cap in the last decade. But inference is much more than calling model.forward. Every token has to move through a complicated stack of routing, caching, scheduling, kernels, memory, and hardware, all while balancing speed, cost, and quality.

We brought together researchers and builders from Together AI, Ollama, Luminal, and SGLang & RadixArk to take us through that stack from end to end. We’ll see how a token gets from an API request to a GPU and back, why the same open model can perform differently depending on who serves it, and how new approaches to compilers and caching are making inference faster and dramatically more efficient.

Join us for the next Paper Club on November 4th, where we'll talk AI for biology: https://events.ycombinator.com/yc-paper-club-nov-4

Chapters:
00:00 - Why inference matters more than training
08:24 - Three kinds of inference innovation
12:14 - Dan Fu: the lifecycle of an inference request
42:18 - Jeff Morgan: not all open model tokens are the same
1:04:31 - Joe Fioti: compiling models with search, not heuristics
1:30:30 - Liangsheng Yin: SGLang and memory for the agent era

videos.title: Video Editing Using Claude AI 🔥 Step-by-Step Tutorial (தமிழில்) | AI Video Editing 2026
videos.description:
Plugin Link:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-9rKCnNKqG6X5l_L_sEDvAf8y27gQeOD/view?usp=sharing

Prompt:
I'm uploading a raw vertical short-form clip Tamil speech. Edit it for maximum
viewer retention using ffmpeg/Python. Do all of this:

1. CUT DEAD AIR: detect silences longer than 0.35s and remove them. Keep 0.08s
   padding so words don't get clipped. Remove obvious retakes/stumbles.
2. HOOK: the first 1.5 seconds must grab attention. Put my strongest line first
   if possible, and add a bold on-screen hook text: "your hook in Tamil".
3. PATTERN INTERRUPTS: every 2–3 seconds add a variation: alternate between
   normal framing and a 1.15x punch-in zoom on my face, cut-synced.
4. TAMIL CAPTIONS: Route A: here is my transcript: paste Tamil text
   Route B: transcribe the audio with Whisper language=ta, show me the
   transcript to correct before burning it in.
   Style: 2–4 words per line, centred in the lower third above the platform UI,
   white text with thick black outline, highlight the key word in yellow.
   Use a proper Tamil font Noto Sans Tamil / Mukta Malar so letters join correctly.
5. PROGRESS BAR: thin bar at the very top that fills over the video's length.
6. AUDIO: normalize loudness to -14 LUFS. If I upload music, duck it to about
   -20 dB under my voice.
7. EXPORT: 1080x1920, H.264, 30fps, MP4, under 60s.

Before rendering, give me the edit plan cuts with timestamps, zoom points,
caption chunks. After rendering, extract 4 frames so we can check framing.

🔥 What You'll Learn

✅ Introduction to Claude AI for Video Editing

✅ Claude Code Installation & Setup

✅ How to Set Up an AI Video Editing Environment

✅ Connecting Claude Code with FFmpeg

✅ Adding Background Music & Transitions

✅ Exporting Your Final Edited Video

✅ Building Your Own AI Video Editing Workflow

Why Use Claude AI for Video Editing?

Claude AI can help generate editing scripts, understand your instructions, automate repetitive tasks, and simplify complex editing workflows.

Instead of manually writing every FFmpeg command, you can describe your editing requirements in natural language and use Claude Code to generate and execute the necessary commands.

Example Prompt:

"Take my raw video, remove unwanted pauses, generate subtitles, normalize audio levels, and export the final video in 1080p using FFmpeg. Show me the editing plan before processing."

Note: Claude does not replace a complete video editor by itself. Actual media processing requires external tools such as FFmpeg, Python, or compatible editing software.
